### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object: one pass, named and unambiguous — "you bought the big Collective Unlimited pass for
yourself in December"; "Asked which pass, you say it is the only one, in your own name, Alan Whitcombe."
Timing: "settled on this call rather than left hanging." Boundary of the action: he asks for the money
side, not for a particular mechanism — "what you want is whatever the collective will put back to you on
that pass" — and he explicitly does not constrain the form: "you are not asking for cash back and you do
not argue about how it comes back … if the agent explains it comes back as resort credit against the
pass you say that is fine." Authorisation: `3035550168` for the lookup, `1971-07-03` and `GR41007391`
(and `80525` as a third) for identity, and blanket consent to the desk doing what is needed — "you say
go ahead, that is what they are there for, and you do not ask what it comes to."

He also consents in advance to the disposal itself, but only if the agent raises it: "If the agent
explains that the pass itself has to be given up before the collective will put anything back, you do
not hesitate: you say yes, give the pass up … and the reason is the job going." He states the ground
(job loss) and the last ski day (3 January) but refuses to guess counts — "you cannot remember exactly
how many and you say so rather than guess" — and refuses to characterise the protection plan — "you do
not know what the plan is called or what it paid … You would rather they read all that off their own
records."

The simulator conveys needs and answers passively, never states a figure, never proposes an order, and
executes a user tool only when one is handed over: "When the agent hands a step over to you and asks you
to do it yourself, you do it with the details they give you"; "you accept it without quarrelling … you
never suggest one of your own."

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and the eligibility grounds

**Act now.** Every visible ground is satisfied at the frozen moment:

- *Inside the cancellation window.* `Giving Up a Granite Ridge Season Pass: Window, Grounds and What
  Comes Back`: "The cancellation is honoured for a refund only when it is recorded no later than the
  cancellation window counted in calendar days from the day the pass application was recorded … the
  boundary day itself satisfies it." `applied_date: '2026-12-09'`; the Collective Unlimited window is 30
  calendar days (`Granite Ridge Season Pass Schedule: Cancellation Window, Fee, Refund Basis and Day Use
  Deduction`); the handling date 2027-01-06 stands 28 days out, inside the window (boundary 2027-01-08).
- *Not a medical cancellation.* The same document gates only medical grounds on a settled claim
  ("A cancellation given on medical grounds is honoured only when …"). The ground here is the job going,
  which the tool's own label set carries as `employment_loss` — "the household has lost the employment
  the pass was bought on". The medical gate is therefore not in issue.
- *Not twice.* "A pass record that already stands in the cancelled or closed state is not cancelled
  again." `status: 'active'`.
- *The form the value comes back in is not the agent's choice.* "What comes back is issued as resort
  credit against the pass record, and a return to the original payment method is a finance team decision
  rather than a desk decision." This matches what he will accept and forecloses paying him cash.
- *Resort credit may still be applied.* `Resort Credit Issued Against a Granite Ridge Season Pass: Terms
  of Use`: "Resort credit is applied only while the pass record it sits on has not reached the cancelled
  or closed state." It has not — yet. This is what makes the ordering in item 6 forced rather than
  merely preferred.

Nothing here is refused and nothing waits on time.

### 4. Each scored parameter: formula in words, inputs, intermediates, value

Published figures used: Collective Unlimited — standard season price 1879.00 (tariff); 8 scheduled
instalments (financing schedule); cancellation window 30, cancellation fee 150.00, refund basis
**pro rata**, day use deduction 169.00 (cancellation schedule); 150 operating days and the season
2026-11-20 → 2027-04-18, i.e. **149 days** (season schedule); smallest single application 50.00 and
validity 365 days (resort credit schedule). From the protection plan's own published schedule, reached
through the runtime retriever: Season Pass Protection Plus has a season limit set at **80.00 per cent**
of covered value and an **excess of 50.00** on every claim.

#### (a) The resort credit applied — **127.57**

`Determination of the Resort Credit Applied in One Application on a Granite Ridge Pass Account`:
"The amount applied is the pot taken at the share drawn and rounded to the cent, less the error credit
held back and less the protection premium held back, the two amounts held back being deducted from that
rounded figure rather than from the pot."

| Step | Rule | This customer | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the pot | baseline: "the resort credit the pass record shows standing" (260.00); tiered by `The Pot a Granite Ridge Resort Credit Application Is Drawn From` | the account shows credit issued to put a billing error right (`credit_reason: 'duplicate_charge'`, which the tool's own label set defines as "credit issued to put right an amount the collective charged twice") → first branch: "every credit entry the pass account shows issued, less every application already drawn" = 260.00 + 45.00, none drawn | **305.00** |
| share drawn | baseline 100 %; tiered by `How Far a Granite Ridge Instalment Schedule Has Run and the Share of the Credit Pot Drawn` | the account shows no scheduled instalment presented and none refused → "three quarters of the pot is drawn" | 75 % → **228.75** |
| error credit held back | baseline: "Nothing is held back"; tiered by `Credit Issued to Put a Billing Error Right on a Granite Ridge Pass Account` | 45.00 of error credit stands and the record still admits the holder (`status: 'active'`) → "the whole of that error credit is held back" | − 45.00 → **183.75** |
| protection premium held back | baseline: "Nothing is held back on that account either"; tiered by `Protection Premium Still to Be Collected and the Granite Ridge Credit Application` | the plan over this pass shows `premium_balance_usd: 56.18` and stands with a settled claim → "The whole of the premium still to be collected is held back" | − 56.18 → **127.57** |
| caps | "never more than the amount the pass account still shows to collect"; "never below the smallest single application" | 127.57 < 1458.68; 127.57 > 50.00 | **127.57** |

The two remaining arguments are also derived rather than guessed. `related_event_id` and `credit_pot`
name *which* entry is being spent, and `Resort Credit Issued Against a Granite Ridge Season Pass: Terms
of Use` settles it: "Where several credit entries sit on one pass, the entry closest to running out is
applied first." Both entries carry the same 365-day validity, so the earlier issue — 2026-12-28,
`0bb40556-f622-405d-928d-dca83fb04cba`, `service_recovery` — is the one closest to running out.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asked for one thing — what comes back to him. Three problems, in this order:

```
  P3  applying resort credit standing on the record   (agent)  <- must be resolved first
   |
  P2  giving the pass up for good                     (user)
   |
  P1  issuing the settlement credit                   (agent)  <- the thing the customer wants
```

**Hop P1 → P2 — state-derived.**
Sentence, in the blocked problem's own document, `Issuing Resort Credit on a Granite Ridge Season Pass
That Has Been Given Up`: *"The resort credit issued when a pass is given up is worked out only after the
pass account carries the charge retained on the pass being given up."* It names a **record-visible
state** — a charge standing on the account — not an action and not a tool; its contract question repeats
it: *"What must the pass account carry before the credit is worked out? The charge retained on the pass
being given up."*
The records say the state does not hold: `find_pass_account_entries` on `624e7ed7-…` returns a plan
opening, six scans and two credit issues, and no retained charge.
Which write brings that charge about is found from the sentence's own words: searching for what places a
charge retained on a pass being given up reaches `Giving Up a Granite Ridge Season Pass for Good`, whose
business effect is the write — *"the charge kept is booked on the pass account dated today"*. Nothing in
P1's documents names that facility, its tool or its policy.

**Hop P2 → P3 — state-derived.**
Sentence, in the blocked problem's own document, `Giving Up a Granite Ridge Season Pass for Good`:
*"The charge retained when a pass is given up is worked out only after the pass account carries an
application of resort credit against the amount it still shows to collect."* Again a record-visible
state.
The records say it does not hold: `pass_credit_usd: 260.0` stands on the record, two
`passes_credit_issue` entries stand on the account, and there is no application entry against them.
Which write brings an application about is found from the plain words the records use for the item —
resort credit standing on the pass record: `Spending Resort Credit Standing on a Granite Ridge Season
Pass Record`, whose business effect is *"One application is booked on the pass account dated today, the
resort credit left on that pass record drops by the figure applied and the amount still to be collected
drops by the same figure."* Nothing in P2's documents names that facility, its tool or its policy.

**P3** carries no prerequisite sentence and the tree terminates.

**Why the order is forced and not merely tidy.** `Resort Credit Issued Against a Granite Ridge Season
Pass: Terms of Use` says "Resort credit is applied only while the pass record it sits on has not reached
the cancelled or closed state", and running `give_up_season_pass_8c1a0eca` moves the record to
`cancelled`. An agent who gave the pass up first would have destroyed its own ability to apply the
credit — and the retained charge would in any case have been computed on the wrong outstanding balance
(1458.68/1458.68 = 1.00, selecting the 1.25 multiple instead of 1.1). The dependency therefore bears
real weight on this task's number, and the visible materials say so without any route being written.

**Hop marks.** P1 → P2 **state-derived**; P2 → P3 **state-derived**. **No hop was pre-solved.**

### Two-way counter-proof

**The closest alternatives are each excluded by a visible sentence or record.**

| Alternative | What excludes it |
| --- | --- |
| Return money to the card | "a return to the original payment method is a finance team decision rather than a desk decision" |
| Record the surrender on medical grounds, or treat the settled claim as the gate | The ground he gives is the job going; `employment_loss` is the label for "the household has lost the employment the pass was bought on". The medical gate applies only to "a cancellation given on medical grounds" |
| Take the pot as the 260.00 the record shows standing | The pot rule's first branch is met — "A record whose running figure has had to be corrected is no longer the authority on what stands" — because a `duplicate_charge` entry stands |
| Draw the whole pot | The schedule-stage rule's first branch is met: no instalment presented, none refused → three quarters |
| Hold back half the error credit, or half the premium | Both 50 % rows are conditioned away: the record still admits the holder, and the plan's claim has been settled |
| Deduct the hold-backs from the pot rather than the drawn figure | "the two amounts held back being deducted from that rounded figure rather than from the pot" |
| Take the day use deduction off the gross amount | The pro rata tier with at least one scan reaches the first branch — "with no day use deduction taken" |
| Measure the season share from the season's opening day | The tier admits on 150 days and the pass became scannable after the season opened, which selects the scannable-day denominator "so that only the part of the season the holder actually had is counted" |
| Count his "handful of days" as five, or count 2026-12-27 once | The rule counts "lift scan entries standing on the pass account", of which there are six, two of them on 2026-12-27 |
| Take half the retained charge off the credit | The 50 % row needs an account with "nothing left to collect"; 1652.81 stands |
| Take half the payout off | The 50 % row is for "a claim still open"; this claim is settled |
| Apply the 1.1 uplift | That row needs "no amount placed on it to be collected by instalments"; 1458.68 was placed |
| Act on the withdrawn `refund_review` request | `outcome: 'withdrawn'`; no document gives a withdrawn request any effect |

**Counter-proof against "do only the one thing the customer asked for".** Calling
`issue_settlement_credit_d3237287` alone is excluded by the visible sentence in its own document — the
credit "is worked out only after the pass account carries the charge retained on the pass being given
up", and no such charge stands. Nor could the figure be right: the retained-charge offset reads "Where
that charge stands on the pass account …", and on an untouched account neither of its conditions is
reached, so nothing would be taken off at all. The governed result would be left in a state the visible
principles do not allow.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Each computation document alone, with the
product figures it names and no factor applied, yields a definite number, and each differs:

| Computation | Fall-back (no factor applied) | Derived answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| credit applied | pot = the 260.00 the record shows standing, drawn in full, nothing held back on either account, under the 1458.68 still to collect and above the 50.00 minimum → **260.00** | 127.57 |
| charge retained | charge base 150.00, both shares at 100 %, no scan component, no allowance, no relief → **150.00** | 321.70 |
| credit issued | share 102/149; 1728.68 × 102/149 = 1183.39, less the day use deduction of 169.00 → **1014.39**; scan share 100 %, nothing off for the retained charge or the payout, uplift ×1 → **1014.39** | 302.90 |

No computation document hints that anything modifies it: each states its baseline flat ("The whole of
the pot is drawn in one application", "Nothing further is retained for the lift scans the pass account
shows", "No uplift is added"), with no exception list and no pointer.

**A cross-product reach, recorded.** `Relief Against a Granite Ridge Retained Charge for Protection Held
Over the Pass` names the plan by its official product name ("a Pass and Trip Protection plan") and names
the three things it reads ("the state it stands in, the share of the covered value its season benefit
runs to, and the excess it carries"), but the excess and the season-benefit share are figures published
in the protection product's own schedule, not in `docs/passes/`. They are findable: `KB_search` on this
task with the plan's words returns `Benefit Shares, Excesses and Caps Under Pass and Trip Protection`
directly, where `Season Pass Protection Plus` carries a season limit at 80.00 per cent of covered value
and an excess of 50.00. I record this as a note on the visible surface rather than as a defect, since
the skill's audit boundary is this product's corpus and the sibling corpus was not used as a criterion —
but the derivation of 321.70 does depend on those two figures.

**Openness recorded as a policy-side note, not a document defect.** As in task 0, "the cycle of the
handling date" is used but nowhere defined in this corpus. It is not load-bearing on this task.

### Every factor tier, checked against the source ladder

| `season_remaining_allowance` | 102 of 149 days left, at least two thirds → 25.00 | same | yes |
| `protection_excess_relief` (cross-difficulty, `insure`) | settled claim with a season benefit at 80 in the hundred of covered value → the plan's excess, 50.00 | same | yes |
| `remaining_share_basis` | tier at 150 days, scannable after the season opened → 102 / 129 | same; baseline 102 / 149 | yes |
| `gross_back_basis` | pro rata basis with at least one scan → price × share, no day use deduction = 1366.86 | same; baseline 1197.86 | yes |
| `scan_share` | 6 scan entries, at least the heavy-use count → 90 % | same | yes |
| `retained_charge_offset` | charge stands and the account still shows an amount to collect → 100 % | same | yes |

| `credit_uplift` | financed and the price still being collected → 1.05 | same | yes |

Every tier selection, every intermediate the documents name, and the fall-back are identical. The single
divergence is arithmetic, and it is isolated below.

### The one divergence — **KB-RUNTIME RED**

**Symptom.** From the published documents alone the settlement credit is **302.90**. The scored value is
**302.89**.

**Where exactly.** In the final assembly, at the product of the gross amount and the scan share.

| | Documents | Source `compute` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gross amount | 1366.86 | 1366.86 (`RND(...,2)`, agreeing) |
| gross × scan share | 1366.86 × 0.90 = **1230.174**, carried unrounded because the document says the figure "is rounded to the cent once at the end" | `RND(gross_back_usd * use_rate, 2)` = **1230.17** |
| less the charge retained, less the payout | 1230.174 − 321.70 − 620.00 = 288.474 | 1230.17 − 321.70 − 620.00 = 288.47 (the source's `plumbing` line records "net_back_usd 288.47 before the uplift") |
| × the uplift, rounded once | 288.474 × 1.05 = 302.8977 → **302.90** | 288.47 × 1.05 = 302.8935 → **302.89** |

**Root cause — on the policy side, not in the rendering.** The source's own `rule` and
`compute_basis['result']` say: *"The amount coming back is the gross amount taken at the scan share, less
the charge retained taken at the offset share and less what the protection plan has paid out taken at the
payout share, and the figure that gives is then taken at the credit uplift; it is rounded to the cent
once at the end and is never below zero."* The source's `compute` rounds three separate products to the
cent before the subtraction and rounds again at the end, i.e. more than once. The charter's prose and the
charter's compute do not agree, and the GT follows the compute.

**Evidence that the documents are a faithful carriage of that prose, so nothing here is a rendering
fault.** `Determination of the Resort Credit Issued on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Given Up` carries the
sentence word for word under **The amount coming back**. No other visible document supplies intermediate
rounding at that step: `Lift Scans Standing on a Granite Ridge Pass Account and the Share Taken of the
Gross Amount` works only exact figures ("A gross amount of 900.00 … taken at 90 per cent, which gives
810.00"); `The Charge Retained on a Granite Ridge Season Pass and the Share Taken Off the Credit Issued`
likewise ("The whole 187.50 is taken off"); `What a Pass and Trip Protection Plan Has Paid Out…` likewise
("half of it is taken off, which is 310.00"); and `The Uplift Added for Taking the Value Back as Granite
Ridge Resort Credit` works 450.60 × 1.05 = 473.13 exactly. The computation document's own worked example
takes the scan share at 100 per cent, so it never exhibits the step either.

**Consequence.** A solver who reads every published document and every record, reasons faultlessly and
makes no arithmetic slip passes `settlement_credit_usd: 302.90` to
`issue_settlement_credit_d3237287`, and the exact-value criterion scores it wrong by one cent. The
conclusion the source scores is explicable only from the hidden `compute`. That is the runtime condition
this part of the audit exists to catch, so it is recorded as **KB-RUNTIME RED** — with its root cause
named as source-layer prose/compute drift, so that it is routed to the layer that can settle which of
the two the charter means. I do not propose the repair, and it does not belong in the documents: the
sentence they carry is the source's own.

*Scope note.* The same class of drift on the carry-forward fee base (recorded in `0.md`) does not change
a scored value on task 0. This one does.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME RED** for task 1, on `settlement_credit_usd` alone. Every other blind item — both other
scored values, all three fall-backs, all sixteen factor tiers, the problem tree, both edges and their
order, the owners and the terminal state — was derived correctly from the runtime-visible materials
alone, before any source artefact was read, and no hop was pre-solved.

## revision_2 / comparison

### Is the round-1 RED genuinely closed?

**Yes, and closed at the level of method rather than of the single figure.**

Round 1 recorded: the documents entail 302.90, the source scores 302.89, because the compute rounded
intermediates the prose said were not rounded. The source author moved the **compute** to the prose —
`RND` removed from `gross_back_usd` and `net_back_usd`, leaving it only on `result` — so the scored value
is now 302.90, which is the figure the documents entail. The document-reader path and the compute path
now run the same method, not merely arrive at the same answer: both carry full precision through the
scan share, the two offsets and the uplift, and both round exactly once at the end.

Three things make me treat this as a real closure rather than a coincidence:

1. **The corpus was also corrected in the same direction**, so the two sides meet in the middle rather
   than the prose alone being declared right. `settlement_credit_basis`'s worked example previously
   demonstrated an intermediate rounding — *"The price committed to multiplied by that share is 599.60
   **when taken to the cent**"* — which under the stripped compute would itself have been a false
   instruction. It has been rebuilt on figures that divide exactly (1490.00 × 60/149 = 600.00, less
   169.00 = 431.00) and now says *"neither figure is rounded at those steps"* and *"Rounded to the cent
   once at the end, and only there"*. That is the stronger repair: the example can no longer teach the
   wrong method on any figures.
2. **The same repair was made to the sibling steps**, not only to the one that failed — see the class
   check below.
3. **The margin is wide** (0.42 of a cent-fraction from the tie), so the agreement does not depend on
   float representation.

### The class check the coordinator asked for: reader and compute across every rounding site

I enumerated every `RND` left in this difficulty's compute and every rounding assertion left in the
corpus, and matched them both ways.

**Surviving `RND` sites — 11, and every one named in prose:**

| Policy | Binding | Sentence that names it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arrears recovery | `instalment_amount` | "divided by the number of instalments the schedule holds, rounded to the cent" |
| arrears recovery | `principal_due` | "and that product is rounded to the cent" |
| arrears recovery | `fee_component` | "multiplied by the share taken, rounded to the cent" |
| arrears recovery | `result` | "the past-due principal plus the fee component, rounded to the cent" |
| reinstatement | `result` | "rounded to the cent only once the reduction has been taken" |
| carry-forward | `result` | "rounded to the cent only once, on that final figure" |
| credit offset | `drawn_usd` | "the pot taken at the share drawn and rounded to the cent" |
| credit offset | `net_application_usd` | "and is rounded to the cent once at the end" |
| credit offset | `result` (minimum fall-back) | **not named** — see the benign gap below |
| cancellation | `result` | "rounded to the cent once at the end" |
| settlement | `result` | "rounded to the cent once at the end, and only there" |

**Rounding assertions left in the corpus — every one maps to a surviving `RND`.** The five that no longer
had one have been removed, and all five were removals of a *render-layer rider*, not of a source clause.
I verified that directly: across all six extended policies, **no factor ladder in the source contains any
rounding language at all**, and every rounding sentence in the source lives in a `rule` or
`baseline.rule`. So the render agent's account — that the clauses were already right and what needed
changing were derived units it had added — is accurate, and I can say so on evidence rather than on its
word. The five removals:

| Document | Rider removed | Binding whose `RND` went |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `billing_error_credit_hold_back` | "and the figure held back is rounded to the cent" | `retained_usd` |
| `protection_premium_hold_back` | "and the figure held back is rounded to the cent" | `premium_hold_usd` |
| `protection_excess_relief` | "rounded to the cent" | `protection_relief_usd` |
| `lift_scan_component` (table row) | "rounded to the cent" | `scan_component_usd` |
| `carry_forward_fee_base` | "the figure is rounded to the cent" | `fee_base_usd` |

**The one unnamed rounding is benign.** `credit_offset.result`'s minimum fall-back,
`RND(MX(0, MN(MN(pot_usd, balance_due), P('credit_minimum_redemption_usd'))), 2)`, rounds a minimum of
three quantities that are each already cent-exact — `pot_usd` comes from `SUM`, which the evaluator
itself returns as `round(s, 2)`; `balance_due` is a stored 2-decimal field; and the minimum application
is a published 2-decimal constant. The rounding cannot move any of them, so no document needs to name it
and no reader can be misled. This is very likely one of the "two apparent gaps both benign" the source
auditor reported; I reached it independently and agree.

### Round-1 policy-side note 1 is also closed

The carry-forward fee base no longer diverges either. `fee_base_usd` lost its `RND`, and
`carry_forward_fee_base` lost the sentence that told the reader to round it. A reader now carries
123.858 and so does the compute, and the basis document's "rounded to the cent only once, on that final
figure" is now literally true of the whole assembly rather than contradicted by it. The scored value is
unchanged at 52.38 — it always was — but the method the two sides run is now the same one.

### Verdict for revision_2

**KB-RUNTIME: PASS** for task 1. The round-1 RED is closed, closed as a class rather than as a case, and
nothing in the re-derivation regressed.
